{

      "login": "luke-jr",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "Advocated for a separate utility rather than adding startup migration code to the daemon"
    }
  ],
  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "c:3268176314",
      "kind": "approach",
      "harm": "Using a startup option for a one-time migration creates redundancy and potential configuration conflicts with existing options like -blocksxor",
      "quote": "I don't like using startup options for one-time operations ... maybe we can bundle this e.g. as part of `bitcoin-util` or a separate `bitcoin-xor-blocks` utility?",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "open",
      "author_replies": [
        "r:4525334593"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "settled_by_id": "",
      "settled_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "c:3305066838",
      "kind": "approach",
      "harm": "Adding one-time migration logic to bitcoind adds unnecessary code to the daemon when a standalone utility requires very little of the existing codebase",
      "quote": "I agree a separate utility for this seems better - this requires very little of the existing codebase, in theory.",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "open",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:3305103297",
        "r:4525334593"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "settled_by_id": "",
      "settled_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:2338622414",
      "kind": "approach",
      "harm": "Reading entire block files into memory at once causes high memory usage on memory-constrained systems",
      "quote": "Rather than reading the entire blockfile into memory at once, consider chunking it",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:2338680285",
        "rc:2342882164",
        "rc:2344324168",
        "rc:2365380262"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:2365380262",
      "settled_by_quote": "took a few suggestion from your branch (chunking, code simplifications)"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:2338618798",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "harm": "Rewriting block files alters their timestamps instead of preserving the original modification times",
      "quote": "Would be good to try to reset the timestamp of new_blocks to match that of old_blocks here.",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:2342880343"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:2342880343",
      "settled_by_quote": "Done, thanks!"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:2338660825",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "harm": "Reobfuscation fails or misbehaves on pruned nodes where blk0000.dat has been deleted",
      "quote": "This doesn't seem like it would work correctly with pruning, when blk0000.dat has been deleted?",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:2342882442"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:2342882442",
      "settled_by_quote": "Good call, changed it back to regex matching"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:2338593448",
      "kind": "interface",
      "harm": "Progress reporting resets when finishing undo files before block files, creating an uneven progress display",
      "quote": "I was surprised when it hit 100% of the undo files then restarted on the block files and was much slower",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:2342879651",
        "rc:2365380262"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:2365380262",
      "settled_by_quote": "grouped the block and undo files for more uniform iteration instead of shuffling"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3399270951",
      "kind": "interface",
      "harm": "Malformed hex key lengths for -reobfuscate-blocks are not treated as fatal errors on startup",
      "quote": "It feels a bit off that getting the length wrong is not fatal.",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3436230263",
        "r:4525334593"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "r:4525334593",
      "settled_by_quote": "Made `-reobfuscate-blocks` parsing stricter: only `0`, empty/`1`, or exact 16-character hex keys are accepted; wrong-length keys now fail early"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3637087440",
      "kind": "safety",
      "harm": "Asserting on filesystem operations aborts the node on exceptional runtime conditions instead of returning or throwing errors",
      "quote": "It does feel a bit weird to me to assert on what is not an invariant of the program, but rather an exceptional condition. Why not just throw or return here",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3649809000"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:3649809000",
      "settled_by_quote": "filesystem failures now propagate instead of aborting on assertions."
    }
  ],

  "notes": "sedited approved the PR after review iterations on startup parsing and filesystem assertion handling. ajtowns' concerns about file chunking, timestamp preservation, and pruning were addressed, while stickies-v and luke-jr's suggestion to implement this as a standalone utility rather than a bitcoind startup flag remains open."

participants.note: Concept ACK and full ACK after startup parsing and filesystem error handling were addressed
Concept ACK, though suggested bundling into a standalone utility instead of a startup flag
Raised concerns regarding file chunking, timestamp preservation, and pruning compatibility
Advocated for a separate utility rather than adding startup migration code to the daemon

claims.harm: Using a startup option for a one-time migration creates redundancy and potential configuration conflicts with existing options like -blocksxor
claims.quote: I don't like using startup options for one-time operations ... maybe we can bundle this e.g. as part of `bitcoin-util` or a separate `bitcoin-xor-blocks` utility?

claims.harm: Adding one-time migration logic to bitcoind adds unnecessary code to the daemon when a standalone utility requires very little of the existing codebase
claims.quote: I agree a separate utility for this seems better - this requires very little of the existing codebase, in theory.

claims.harm: Reading entire block files into memory at once causes high memory usage on memory-constrained systems
claims.quote: Rather than reading the entire blockfile into memory at once, consider chunking it
claims.settled_by_quote: took a few suggestion from your branch (chunking, code simplifications)

claims.harm: Rewriting block files alters their timestamps instead of preserving the original modification times
claims.quote: Would be good to try to reset the timestamp of new_blocks to match that of old_blocks here.

claims.harm: Reobfuscation fails or misbehaves on pruned nodes where blk0000.dat has been deleted
claims.quote: This doesn't seem like it would work correctly with pruning, when blk0000.dat has been deleted?
claims.settled_by_quote: Good call, changed it back to regex matching

claims.harm: Progress reporting resets when finishing undo files before block files, creating an uneven progress display
claims.quote: I was surprised when it hit 100% of the undo files then restarted on the block files and was much slower
claims.settled_by_quote: grouped the block and undo files for more uniform iteration instead of shuffling

claims.harm: Malformed hex key lengths for -reobfuscate-blocks are not treated as fatal errors on startup
claims.quote: It feels a bit off that getting the length wrong is not fatal.
claims.settled_by_quote: Made `-reobfuscate-blocks` parsing stricter: only `0`, empty/`1`, or exact 16-character hex keys are accepted; wrong-length keys now fail early

claims.harm: Asserting on filesystem operations aborts the node on exceptional runtime conditions instead of returning or throwing errors
claims.quote: It does feel a bit weird to me to assert on what is not an invariant of the program, but rather an exceptional condition. Why not just throw or return here
claims.settled_by_quote: filesystem failures now propagate instead of aborting on assertions.

support.reason: this seems like useful functionality to expose.
The migration logic looks nice, and while a C++ standalone utility would be a good candidate later, the PR should not be blocked on pioneering GUI launching and lock handling.

result.notes: sedited approved the PR after review iterations on startup parsing and filesystem assertion handling. ajtowns' concerns about file chunking, timestamp preservation, and pruning were addressed, while stickies-v and luke-jr's suggestion to implement this as a standalone utility rather than a bitcoind startup flag remains open.
